interest: Shows Depression-era Japanese silk filature credit dependency and a controversial 1932 government silk sale to Gerli.
overview: Two 1932 cross-reference sheets: Neville's telegram notes silk filatures depend on seasonal bank loans to buy cocoons, while his despatch reports the Japanese government's disruptive sale of silk reserves to American dealer Paolino Gerli.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Japan

people.name: Paolino Gerli
people.role: American silk merchant and buyer of Japanese government silk stocks

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram regarding the agricultural nature of the silk industry and the financing of cocoon purchases by filatures.
subfiles.summary: Neville's April 1932 telegram notes Japan's silk industry remains agricultural, with filatures buying farmers' cocoons dependent on recurring bank loans each season.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Telegram No. 107 from Neville on silk industry financing

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a report on the Japanese Government's sale of silk to Paolino Gerli and resultant industry complications.
subfiles.summary: Neville's June 1932 despatch reports the Japanese government's sale of silk reserves to American dealer Paolino Gerli caused severe disruption across the silk industry.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 634 from Neville on government silk sale to Paolino Gerli
